title: Routing policy mismatch causing customer requests to be served by wrong model/region/tier
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Multiple paying customers reported user-facing regressions where requests were routed to incorrect model variants, wrong regions, or downgraded capacity tiers. The misroutes affected hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments depending on the customer routing policy configuration and caused increased latency, failed SLOs, and in one case data residency concerns.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer routing policy with: primary model = redwood/gpt-3-x, fallback chain = [redwood/gpt-3-x-quant, redwood/gpt-3-s], preferred_region = eu-west-1, tier_preference = [dedicated, hosted]
2) Simulate capacity pressure in eu-west-1 dedicated pool and mark dedicated as 'unavailable' for that customer (via canary toggles used in testing)
3) Send a steady stream of requests with varying prompt lengths and client-provided region hints

4) Observe that some requests are routed to a hosted low-cost model in us-east-1 despite the policy preferring dedicated eu-west-1 then hosted eu-west-1; user-visible latency and embedding-quality regressions appear
5) Reproducible when routing cache is warm and when the request path goes through policy evaluation + cached decision path
observed_behavior: Routing decision engine selected a model variant that did not meet the customer's region and tier constraints under capacity pressure. The fallback comparator allowed a hosted variant in a different region and lower tier because its "cost_score" was evaluated without considering region/tier hard constraints. The cache layer then persisted that decision for subsequent requests.
expected_behavior: Routing must respect hard constraints (region, customer-tier) before applying soft scores (cost/latency). Fallbacks should only consider variants that match region/tier unless the customer's policy explicitly allows cross-region or lower-tier fallthrough.
root_cause:
Two contributing issues identified:
- A regression in the fallback comparator introduced in runtime-1.20 where the comparator reduced the constraint tuple to (model_alias, cost_score) and dropped region/tier from the ordering key. This allowed cheaper cross-region variants to win when cost_score delta exceeded threshold.
- The routing cache key omitted region and tier constraints for entries created by the policy evaluator under high load, causing the cross-region decision to be reused for requests that should have been isolated by region.
mitigation_taken:
- Immediate mitigation: disabled aggressive cost-based scoring for affected customer policies via feature flag and purged routing cache for impacted customers (manual purge script).
- Short-term: pushed a hotfix to the policy evaluator to reintroduce region+tier back into the decision tuple and to add a safety check that rejects cross-region variants unless explicitly allowed.
- Communication: Notified impacted customers via support and posted incident notes with workarounds (pin model version or restrict fallbacks).
fix_summary: Code changes in routing-service: restore strict constraint ordering by including (region, tier, model_alias) into the decision key, update comparator unit tests, and modify cache key generation to include region and effective tier. Added canary gating and a feature flag to roll back aggressive cost scoring. Added end-to-end tests that simulate dedicated pool unavailability and assert region fidelity.
deploy_plan: 1) Merge PRs and run CI (unit+integration+e2e). 2) Deploy hotfix to staging and run synthetic load with dedicated pool failover tests. 3) Gradual canary to 5% production traffic for 1 hour, monitor routing fidelity dashboards and SLOs. 4) Expand to 50% after 2 hours if no regressions, then full rollout. 5) Post-deploy cache sweep for all affected customers.
monitoring_and_rollout_checks: routing-decision-fidelity (per-customer) should report 0 cross-region misroutes for pinned policies
latency p95 should not regress >10% compared to baseline
no increase in 5xx errors for routing-service
postmortem_actions: Add unit+integration tests covering cache key composition and comparator ordering
Create a lint rule to prevent comparator PRs that remove constraint fields without explicit justification
Instrument request lineage: add tags to decisions to show which constraint was decisive
Update runbook: procedures for cache purge and emergency rollback for routing cache
customer_communication: 2026-03-10 15:12 UTC: initial notification to CS and impacted customers acknowledging an issue and describing temporary mitigation
2026-03-11 02:40 UTC: follow-up describing hotfix timeline and workaround to pin models
2026-03-14 09:00 UTC: confirmation of deployment to 100% and request for verification from customers
notes: Root cause spans both policy comparator logic and cache plumbing — two teams involved: routing-service and cache-service

Private deployments required a different remediation path: customers with on-prem routing control were given a patch bundle (runtime patch + routing-service update) and instructions for a rolling restart
We found one regression introduced by a refactor that simplified comparator signature; revert contained detailed comment explaining why region/tier are 'hard' constraints
Follow-up: evaluate whether additional telemetry (e.g., decision_reason tags) should be retained for 30 days for troubleshooting
final_status_notes: Hotfix merged and fully rolled out on 2026-03-14. Monitoring shows misroutes dropped to zero for previously impacted customers. Follow-up work scheduled to harden tests and add decision telemetry. Status: In Progress (deploy verification and postmortem actions in parallel).
